summary.headline: TCI Express Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 10.8% YoY to INR 43 crore with margin at 12.7%, guiding 14-15% growth and 13%+ margin for H2.
summary.overview: Standalone income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 336 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up around 11% to INR 43 crore and margin expanding to 12.7% from 12.4%, the highest in five quarters. PAT rose 6% to INR 27 crore and H1 PAT rose 6% to INR 49 crore. Management said volumes were 265,000 tonnes, up 7.5% YoY, and that October was strong. The call focused on the growth of E-Commerce Express and air/rail services, capex for sorting centres, and competitive pressure from aggregators, which management said is not affecting B2B pricing.

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest business, grew around 9%+ YoY in Q2 and H1. Management said it expects total growth of 14-15% in H2 with volume growth of 11-12%.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew about 29% YoY; management is building a separate air network covering about 20 cities.

segments.name: E-Commerce Express
segments.commentary: Grew about 52% YoY (company said 51.6%). Management describes it as a small business and is focusing on D2C, small e-commerce players and Tier 2 cities; target EBITDA margin of 15%.

segments.name: C2C Express
segments.commentary: Declined YoY because fuel-price volatility made rates unattractive; management expects growth to resume from Q3.

segments.name: Rail (express parcel)
segments.commentary: Growing and being built as a separate network from railway stations; management cites 99% delivery service level. No figure given.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue growth guided at 14-15%, with volume growth around 11-12%.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 13%+; management expects margin expansion of at least 50-100 bps for FY27 over FY26.
Price increases net around 1.5% after passing through fuel costs; management expects price hikes to continue in Q3 and Q4.
Share of non-Surface services (Air Express, International Air, Rail, E-Commerce, C2C) is about 17-17.5%; target is 18%+ by FY27 year-end and above 22% by 2030.

Capex plan of about INR 100 crore+ per year over the next four to five years, with conversion of 12-15 sorting centres (6-7 done, 3 more by FY27 end), and three major locations (Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore) over three to four years.
capex_capacity: Tonnage in Q2 was 265,000 tonnes, up 7.5% YoY; capacity utilisation was not quantified.
Current INR 400 crore capex programme (cut from INR 500 crore) is about INR 80 crore spent in H1, with INR 40-50 crore remaining to finish in FY27.
Three new centres (Lucknow, Ahmedabad, Kolkata) to be ready by FY27 year-end; corporate office construction ongoing; automation at Ahmedabad and Kolkata to finish by Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Two automated sorting centres cut labour and truck turnaround time, saving at least 40-50 bps of direct cost per annum, per management.
Management plans to move from leased to owned centres, targeting 80-85% of revenue through owned centres by end-2030 or 2031. Only one centre is promoter-owned.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing is not a talking point in the industry and no one is asking for price cuts; freight is about 1.5% of cargo value.
Management says aggregator and app-based platforms mainly serve B2C, and B2B customers deal directly, so there is no demand impact on Surface Express.

E-Commerce strategy: focus on D2C, merchant connections and small e-commerce players, Tier 2 cities (Surat, Ludhiana, Bengaluru), and profitable business only. SME vs large account split stayed at 50:50.
A digital wallet for e-commerce bookings was signed and is being integrated, with booking expected from next year.
Management said October was strong and the H2 pipeline is robust across all service lines.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of aggregators such as Shiprocket on volumes and on Surface Express?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aggregators mainly affect B2C; B2B customers contact TCI directly, so there is no impact on Surface Express. TCI also registers with aggregators, but this is a small part of E-Commerce Express.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide to 14-15% growth in H2 and is the pricing premium intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 14-15% growth and 11-12% volume growth for H2, with net price increases of about 1.5% and no industry price cuts. Non-Surface services are only 1-2 points of the mix, so Surface Express growth is about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and returns on converted sorting centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans about INR 100 crore+ per year, and automated centres have cut direct cost by 40-50 bps. Returns are initially weighing on ROI and expected to improve over 20-25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did C2C Express decline and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: C2C declined because fuel-price volatility made rates unattractive; rates have normalised and management expects growth to return from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Indian Railway's own parcel booking services a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Railway cannot do door-to-door collection and has only 30-45 minutes to unload at stations, so TCI sees it as a complement to its branch network with 99% service level.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin does E-Commerce Express target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 15% EBITDA margin on D2C accounts and aims to return to 15-16% over two to three years, declining to take business below that.

risks_watch: H2 guidance of 14-15% revenue growth needs a sharp step-up from H1 growth of 8.8%.
Capex returns are still weak; management acknowledges the ROI drag will persist until the new centres and business ramp up.
E-Commerce Express is small and dependent on margin discipline; management is selective about which business to take.
Watch the Q3 C2C Express recovery and whether price hikes of about 1.5% hold amid fuel-price volatility.
Watch the timing of sorting centre commissioning (Lucknow, Ahmedabad, Kolkata) and the automation go-live in Q1-Q2 FY28.
Competition from aggregators and the Indian Railway's own express booking push; management denies any impact so far.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the H2 growth recovery, backed by specific targets, though several answers on competition and pricing were broad and lacked hard data. Management was more cautious on capex returns, acknowledging that ROI is weighing on the business for now.
key_quotes: We delivered another quarter of profitable growth with EBITDA up 10.8% year-on-year and margin expanding to 12.7%, our best in five quarters.
We committed double-digit volume growth and revenue growth.
pricing in this industry is really not a talking point, basically, where people don't want to reduce these prices.
Certainly, I think we will be having a growth of 14%, 15% + in next two quarters, with the volume growth of around what we committed around 11% -12%.

growth.why: Management reiterated H2 FY27 revenue growth of 14-15% on 11-12% volume growth and 13%+ EBITDA margin, backed by price hikes (~1.5% net) and sorting-centre capex (INR 400 cr programme, ~INR 80 cr spent in H1), but no quantified capacity or order book was given and utilisation was not stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 12.7% (highest in five quarters) and H2 guided at 13%+, with at least 50-100 bps FY27 expansion, supported by automated centres cutting direct cost 40-50 bps p.a.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new centres (Lucknow, Ahmedabad, Kolkata) are under the INR 400 crore programme with INR 40-50 crore left to spend in FY27, and utilisation was not quantified so the need is not confirmed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 tonnage 265,000 t was up 7.5% YoY and management guided H2 volume growth of 11-12%, against H1 revenue growth of only 8.8%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management plans INR 100 crore+ capex per year for four to five years, with H1 FY27 spend of about INR 80 crore and utilisation not stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H2 revenue growth of 14-15% needs a sharp step-up from H1's 8.8%, so an upgrade looks unlikely; management reiterated rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Surface Express grew about 9% in Q2 and H1 total growth was 8.8%, so the 14-15% H2 target depends on C2C recovering from Q3 and on price hikes of about 1.5% holding amid fuel volatility.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A digital wallet for e-commerce bookings is being integrated with booking expected from next year, and a separate air network covering about 20 cities is being built; no firm launch date was given.

rows.label: Automated sorting centres cut direct cost
rows.why: Two automated centres have saved at least 40-50 bps of direct cost per year, and Ahmedabad and Kolkata automation is due to finish by Q1 or Q2 FY28.

rows.label: Net price increases of about 1.5%
rows.why: Management expects net price hikes of about 1.5% after fuel pass-through to continue in Q3 and Q4, and says no industry price cuts are being sought.

rows.label: C2C Express recovery
rows.why: C2C declined YoY on fuel volatility, and management says rates have normalised and growth resumes from Q3.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins (13%+ H2 guide) and the 14-15% H2 growth reiteration, but cautious on capex returns and gave broad, data-light answers on aggregator competition and pricing.
